text: Choose the completion describing an imagined discovery before yesterday's publication. We published the error yesterday because nobody checked the figures. If we had checked them, we ___ the error before publication.
focusKey: coverage-conditionals-b2-901:Completed past result of a counterfactual condition
explanation: Would have found places the imagined discovery in the completed past, following the unreal past condition.

rationales.will find: Will find predicts a discovery after now, not before yesterday's publication.
rationales.would find: Would find does not express the required completed result before the past publication.
rationales.would have found: Would have found places the imagined discovery in the completed past, following the unreal past condition.
rationales.have found: Have found reports a real discovery with present relevance, not the imagined alternative.

focusKey: coverage-conditionals-b2-902:Negative passive past counterfactual
explanation: Hadn't been cancelled imagines reversing the completed past cancellation.

rationales.isn't cancelled: Isn't cancelled presents an open current condition, not an alternative to the stated past cancellation.
rationales.wasn't being cancelled: This leaves an ongoing past cancellation process open; it does not reverse the known completed cancellation as requested.
rationales.hasn't been cancelled: Hasn't been cancelled leaves cancellation open up to now, conflicting with the known past cancellation.
rationales.hadn't been cancelled: Hadn't been cancelled imagines reversing the completed past cancellation.

sentence: 'I didn't save a copy. If I had saved one, I could have restored the file.'
setupText: Choose the statement supported by the speaker's account.
taskText: 'I didn't save a copy. If I had saved one, I could have restored the file.'
text: Choose the statement supported by the speaker's account. 'I didn't save a copy. If I had saved one, I could have restored the file.'
options: Saving a copy would have made restoration possible.
The speaker restored the file from a saved copy.
Saving a copy would have required restoration.
The speaker is unsure whether a copy was saved.
answer: Saving a copy would have made restoration possible.
focusKey: coverage-conditionals-b2-903:Could have as unreal past ability
explanation: 'Could have restored' describes an ability that the imagined saved copy would have provided.

rationales.Saving a copy would have made restoratio: 'Could have restored' describes an ability that the imagined saved copy would have provided.
rationales.The speaker restored the file from a sav: The speaker explicitly says no copy was saved and does not report restoration.
rationales.Saving a copy would have required restor: 'Could' expresses possibility or ability, not a requirement to restore.
rationales.The speaker is unsure whether a copy was: The first sentence explicitly states that no copy was saved.

rationales.would not have missed: Would not have missed gives the confident negative past result intended by the guide.
rationales.may have missed: 'May have missed' expresses uncertainty about missing, not the guide's firm alternative outcome.
rationales.would have missed: Would have missed predicts the very failure the guide says the shortcut would have prevented.

rationales.has approved: Has approved reports actual approval, contradicting the rejection.
rationales.might have approved: Might have approved presents approval as a possible unreal past outcome without guaranteeing it.
rationales.must have approved: 'Must have approved' expresses a strong deduction about actual approval, not an uncertain alternative.

sentence: 'If Ana took the nine o'clock train, she should be here by now. I don't know which train she took.'
setupText: Choose the interpretation of this open condition about a past event.
taskText: 'If Ana took the nine o'clock train, she should be here by now. I don't know which train she took.'
text: Choose the interpretation of this open condition about a past event. 'If Ana took the nine o'clock train, she should be here by now. I don't know which train she took.'
options: The speaker uses a possible past fact to estimate Ana's arrival.
The speaker knows Ana missed the nine o'clock train.
The speaker imagines changing Ana's known departure time.
The speaker is instructing Ana to take the next train.
answer: The speaker uses a possible past fact to estimate Ana's arrival.
focusKey: coverage-conditionals-b2-908:Open past condition supporting a present inference
explanation: 'Took' refers to an uncertain past fact; the result is an expectation about now.

rationales.The speaker knows Ana missed the nine o': The final sentence explicitly leaves Ana's train unknown.
rationales.The speaker uses a possible past fact to: 'Took' refers to an uncertain past fact; the result is an expectation about now.
rationales.The speaker imagines changing Ana's know: No departure time is known to be false, so this is not an imagined reversal of a known fact.
rationales.The speaker is instructing Ana to take t: The sentence assesses an arrival; it gives Ana no instruction.

rationales.would have been driving: Would have been driving places an imagined ongoing activity at noon yesterday.
rationales.would have started driving: This locates the start at noon rather than viewing the drive as already in progress.

sentence: 'But for your warning, I would have signed the wrong document.'
setupText: Choose the sentence with the same counterfactual meaning.
taskText: 'But for your warning, I would have signed the wrong document.'
text: Choose the sentence with the same counterfactual meaning. 'But for your warning, I would have signed the wrong document.'
options: Because you warned me, I signed the wrong document.
Even if you had warned me, I would have signed the wrong document.
Unless you had stayed silent, I would have signed the wrong document.
If you hadn't warned me, I would have signed the wrong document.
answer: If you hadn't warned me, I would have signed the wrong document.
focusKey: coverage-conditionals-b2-912:But for as an implicit unreal condition
explanation: 'But for your warning' means 'without that warning'; the if-clause makes the absent-warning alternative explicit.

rationales.Because you warned me, I signed the wron: This makes the warning cause the mistake, reversing its protective role.
rationales.If you hadn't warned me, I would have si: 'But for your warning' means 'without that warning'; the if-clause makes the absent-warning alternative explicit.
rationales.Even if you had warned me, I would have: Even if says the warning would not have prevented the mistake.
rationales.Unless you had stayed silent, I would ha: Unless you had stayed silent applies when there was a warning, reversing the original condition.

rationales.should: 'Should' in this if-clause means if the need happens to arise.

sentence: 'We will consider an application only if both references arrive.'
setupText: Choose the statement guaranteed by the rule, without adding an extra promise.
taskText: 'We will consider an application only if both references arrive.'
text: Choose the statement guaranteed by the rule, without adding an extra promise. 'We will consider an application only if both references arrive.'
